domain: mining dam safety regulation - tailings-dam emergency-status transition prediction (Brazil, ANM SIGBM registry + monthly safety bulletins, dam-month panel 2021-2026)
prediction_question: At the publication instant of ANM's monthly dam-safety bulletin for month M (published in the first days of month M+1, reporting every registered dam's Nivel de Emergencia as of 01/(M+1)), predict for each dam enrolled in the PNSB whether its emergency status (Nivel de Alerta / Emergencia 1-3 vs Sem emergencia) will CHANGE during calendar month M+2, using registry attributes (construction method incl. upstream a montante, material, height, volume, mineral, UF, population downstream), the dam's own published level history from prior bulletins, and current CRI/DPA classification. A useful prediction supports ANM's remote-inspection prioritization (fiscalizacao remota, the bulletin's own producing unit) and civil-defence readiness before a dam's emergency declaration changes, the moment agency resources get reallocated.
prediction_time: Publication of the monthly Boletim Mensal de Seguranca de Barragens de Mineracao for reference month M. Each bulletin states its reference window explicitly ('Os dados analisados neste boletim referem-se as atualizacoes ocorridas entre 01/10/2026 e 01/11/2026') and is published 4-7 days after the window closes (archive page: Outubro 2026 published 05/11/2026 12h45; Setembro 2026 published 06/10/2026). At the instant the predictor knows: the full per-dam level lists as of 01/(M+1) (bulletin tables 5-8), the month-M transition table (bulletin table 4: dams with level changed during M, previous -> current, no per-dam event dates), and registry attributes. The target month M+2 opens at 01/(M+2), strictly after the instant; the M+1 intermediate month is skipped because its transition table is not yet published and its table cannot be split into before/after-instant events (no dated events) - see notes.md 'timing' for the dated example. Timezone: America/Sao_Paulo (federal publications carry no timezone; declared Brazilia time).
target_definition: Binary, per dam: the dam's emergency status in bulletin M+2's per-dam level lists (state as of 01/(M+3)) differs from its state at 01/(M+2) as recorded in bulletin M+1 - i.e. any change (entry into Alerta/Emergencia, escalation, or exit) during calendar month M+2. Variants to measure at construction: entry-or-escalation only; Alerta-or-Emergencia entry from Sem emergencia only. Label sources are the bulletin level lists and the bulletin 'Barragens com situacao de alerta ou emergencia alterada' transition tables; both are excludable from the shipped features. Population: dams enrolled in the PNSB (461 of 908 in the current registry; all 77 dams currently in Alerta/Emergencia are PNSB dams - measured).

jurisdiction.publisher: Agencia Nacional de Mineracao (ANM), Brazilian federal mining regulator; dataset catalogued on the national open-data portal dados.gov.br by CGU (Controladoria-Geral da Uniao)

licence_note: CC-BY (Creative Commons Attribution) on the publisher's own catalog record for the registry data, plus an explicit per-document reproduction grant in every sampled bulletin ('reproducao de dados ... permitida desde que citada a fonte'). Binding condition: attribution of ANM as source. The bulletins additionally carry 'Todos os direitos reservados' over the document itself - so bulletins must be cited/quoted, not re-hosted; only extracted data ships, which the reproduction sentence permits. No share-alike, no NC restriction, no third-party rights (the registry and bulletins are ANM's own operational compilations).
license_evidence: dados.gov.br package record read 2026-11-07 via the portal's own API (https://dados.gov.br/api/publico/conjuntos-dados/barragens-de-mineracao, fetched through the supported browser because the /api/3/action CKAN endpoint is CloudFront-blocked for plain HTTP clients): '"license_id": "cc-by", "license_title": "Creative Commons Attribution"'. The public dataset page (https://dados.gov.br/dados/conjuntos-dados/barragens-de-mineracao) states 'Licenca: Creative Commons Attribution'.

Boletim Mensal Outubro 2026 PDF (https://www.gov.br/anm/pt-br/assuntos/barragens/boletim-de-barragens-de-mineracao/boletim-mensal-outubro-2026.pdf, read 2026-11-07): 'Todos os direitos reservados. E permitida a reproducao de dados e de informacoes contidos nesta publicacao, desde que citada a fonte.' Identical sentence present in the Janeiro 2021 issue ('...desde que citada a fonte') and the Junho 2023 issue (as a standalone heading 'E permitida a reproducao de dados e de informacoes contidas nesta publicacao, desde que citada a fonte').

No personal data in the shipped features: the registry identifies dams and corporate entrepreneurs (CPF_CNPJ of companies), not natural persons; dam names, companies, municipalities and technical attributes only. CNPJ is a public company identifier; CPF entries are sole-proprietor business IDs published by the regulator itself.

measurements.identity_resolution_probe_2026_11_07: Matching bulletin rows to registry rows on normalized (Nome, UF, Municipio): 13/15 sampled dams (11 Tabela-4 transition dams from Outubro 2026 + 4 level-list dams incl. small garimpo dams in RO/AP/RS) matched a UNIQUE registry row; 2 misses are name variants ('Portal' VALE/MG/Itabira - Vale has multiple dams in Itabira; bulletin 'Barragem Serra Azul' vs registry name variant for the ArcelorMittal Itatiaiuco dam). Probe: candidates/anm-sigbm-emergency-transition/probe_registry_mix.py --identity. Conclusion: key join works with exact normalization for most dams; construction needs a documented fallback (fuzzy + entrepreneur + manual disambiguation) and must measure residual unmatched rates per year.
measurements.extraction_cost_measured: one 3.4 MB CSV (2 HTTP requests incl. one WAF-rejected, ~1.6 s each on the coordinator container) + per-bulletin PDFs of 300-700 KB text-extractable via the standard web extraction path (3 sampled: all fully text-extractable, tables and per-dam lists intact); ~64 bulletins ~ 20-40 MB total for the full ledger - a worker job, but small

split_strategy: PLANNED (not yet computed - this is the open item blocking 'ready'): temporal by calendar month of the target window over the dam-month panel 2021-2026, e.g. train 2021-2023, eval 2024, holdout 2025-Out/2026; both classes must be present in every window with counts computed from the actual ledger. Clustering is expected and must be reported: dams cluster by entrepreneur (Vale alone accounts for many transitions) and municipality (e.g. the Itabira/Mariana/Brumadinho clusters; Nova Lima and Nossa Senhora do Livramento have multi-dam entrepreneurs), so cluster-robust intervals at entrepreneur level are required. The 2022 Jun-Nov archive gap censors those transitions: consecutive-month diffs are only usable where both bulletins exist.
next_action: Worker ledger job (no new source access needed; all inputs are the pinned CSV + the ~64 enumerated bulletin PDFs): (1) enumerate the three archive pages, verify the first issue and the exact 2022 gaps; (2) parse per-dam level lists per bulletin (every era sampled has them) and the transition tables where present; (3) build dam x month state panel by differencing consecutive issues, join registry rows on normalized (Nome, UF, Municipio) with the documented fallbacks, measure unmatched rates; (4) compute the split windows' positive/negative counts for the primary label and the entry-only variant, with entrepreneur-clustered counts; (5) record those counts in split_strategy and, if all five contracts stand, advance the record to 'ready' before construction. Also opportunistic: re-probe https://app.anm.gov.br/SIGBM/Publico from the worker (coordinator connections are closed) to check the Power BI 'historicos' panels for per-dam dated level history - if dated events exist, the M+1 skip-buffer can be replaced by exact event-date timing.
verdict: promising - one measured prerequisite (ledger split counts) stands between this record and 'ready'
